import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 931

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
-/

namespace Erdos931

/--
Let $k_1 \geq k_2 \geq 3$. Are there only finitely many $n_2\geq n_1 + k_1$
such that
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq k_1}(n_1 + i)\ \text{and}\ \prod_{1\leq j\leq k_2} (n_2 + j)
$$
have the same prime factors?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_931 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k₁ : ℕ) (k₂ ≥ 3), k₂ ≤ k₁ →
    { (n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
      (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors }.Finite := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős thought perhaps if the two products have the same factors then
$n_2 > 2(n_1 + k_1)$.
It is an open question whether this is true when allowing a finite number of counterexamples.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_931.variants.additional_condition : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k₁ : ℕ) (k₂ ≥ 3), k₂ ≤ k₁ →
    {(n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧
      (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Finite := by
  sorry

/--
In fact there exist counterexamples, like this one found by AlphaProof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_931.variants.additional_condition_nonempty : ∃ (k₁ k₂ : ℕ), ∃ (_h₁ : k₂ ≤ k₁), ∃ (_h₂ : 3 ≤ k₂),
  {(n₁, n₂) | n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧
      (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Nonempty := by
  use 10, 3, (by norm_num), (by norm_num)
  use (0, 13)
  norm_num [Finset.prod_Icc_succ_top]
  norm_num +decide [Nat.primeFactors, Nat.primeFactorsList]

/--
Erdős was unable to prove that if the two products have the same factors
then there must exist a prime between $n_1$ and $n_2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_931.variants.exists_prime (k₁ k₂ n₁ n₂ : ℕ) (h₁ : k₂ ≤ k₁) (h₂ : 3 ≤ k₂)
    (h₃ : n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂) (h₄ : (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors =
      (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors) :
    ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ n₁ ≤ p ∧ p ≤ n₂ := by
  sorry

end Erdos931

reformulations.difference: The source asks for finitely many possible n₂, whereas Lean asserts finiteness of the set of pairs (n₁,n₂).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Projection onto n₂ preserves finiteness. Conversely, for each fixed n₂ the condition n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ bounds n₁ by n₂, so the fiber contains only finitely many pairs. A finite set of possible n₂ therefore gives a finite union of finite fibers. This equivalence was proved for an arbitrary additional predicate in Review931.finite_pairs_iff_finite_seconds.

reformulations.difference: The source discusses n₂ > 2(n₁+k₁) with finitely many exceptions; Lean asserts finiteness of the admissible pairs satisfying the opposite, non-strict inequality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed k₁,k₂, the displayed set is exactly the set where the implication from non-overlap and equal prime factors to 2*(n₁+k₁) < n₂ fails. Its finiteness is equivalent to that implication holding outside a finite exceptional set. Both the identification of the exception set and its equivalence to eventual truth in the cofinite filter were proved in /workspace/review/finiteness.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean asks for a prime in the closed interval [n₁,n₂]. The primary source says that the products cannot have the same prime factors if n₁ and n₂ are both between the same two consecutive primes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under n₂ ≥ n₁+k₁ and k₁ ≥ 3, absence of a prime in [n₁,n₂] is equivalent to both endpoints lying strictly inside a single consecutive-prime gap. For n₁ ≤ 2, the interval already contains the prime 2. Otherwise, the greatest prime below n₁ and the least prime above n₂ establish the converse. Contraposition therefore gives precisely Lean's closed-interval conclusion; replacing both bounds with strict inequalities is not required by the original wording. This equivalence, including the small boundary cases and an instantiation with the file's hypotheses, was proved in /workspace/review/primegap.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf — P. Erdős, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions (1976), p. 29, equation (10) and following paragraph
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2507.09899 — N. Lebowitz-Lockard, On pairs of consecutive sequences with the same radicals, especially §4

review.notes: Checked all four declarations, including answer scope, quantifier bounds, product indexing, satisfiability, and boundary cases. The webpage records the main question as open and explicitly confirms the AlphaProof counterexample to the stronger exception-free inequality; that counterexample does not contradict the finite-exception variant. Nat.primeFactors has the intended distinct-prime-divisor semantics here because both products are positive. Independently verified the AlphaProof example, Tijdeman's example, and a matching pair with k₁=k₂=3. The existing counterexample proof and the scratch equivalence proofs depend only on standard Lean axioms, not sorryAx. Scratch checks are in /workspace/review/{scratch,finiteness,primegap}.lean. The reviewed file's hash matches the committed file.
